question: Does an NFL season's 18-feature profile predict next season's PPR points-per-game beyond what this season's PPR already predicts?
verdict: 0 of 4 positions earn it: none. The PER-POSITION rows are the finding; the pooled row is reported and is confounded.
cut_sweep_changed_a_verdict: TE cleared both bars on the single 2018 cut — gain +0.0105 against a 0.01 threshold at p=0.000 — and would have shipped as 'the tight-end profile forecasts next season'. At the 2021 cut the same gain is -0.0022. A result that changes sign with where the boundary was drawn is a fact about the boundary. The first version of this file had no sweep; build_tennis_forward.py already had one for this reason, so its absence here was an omission rather than a difference between the sports.
qb_note: The profile makes QB prediction WORSE (-0.0151, p=0.500 — the null beats the real gain half the time), and QB persistence is itself the weakest at 0.4914 against 0.74-0.77 elsewhere. QB output is the least self-similar season to season, and the volume-dominated features add noise on the smallest sample.
why_per_position_is_the_finding: Pooling QB/RB/WR/TE puts a 14.48-mean population beside a 5.86-mean one, and the 18 features are z-scored WITHIN SEASON ACROSS ALL FOUR positions, so PASS_ATT_PG is strongly negative for every non-QB. A ridge can recover position from them almost exactly, and 'the model knows a quarterback is a quarterback' would be reported as forecasting skill. Pooled persistence is 0.8 against per-position 0.4914-0.7731 [CORRECTED: this sentence said 0.7642 against 0.58-0.74; neither is in this file's fields — see CORRECTION_why_per_position_prose_numbers_are_stale. The gap is LARGER than the original text claimed] for exactly that reason.
merged_name_note: vectors.json has NO player key — `id` is a row index, 10,700 distinct over 10,700 rows, and 2,014 names own more than one. 227 of 7262 name-keyed pairs join two different people across the season boundary. Excluded via merged_names() in build_vor_draft_value.py, the one gridiron normaliser, which applies the gsis and Wikidata acquittals internally.
min_games_note: Pre-registered before the run, not tuned. A 2-game season's per-game rate is mostly noise, and noise in the target depresses baseline and model equally. Unfiltered pooled persistence is reported alongside so the effect is visible.
era_note: Features are z-scored within season, so a 1999 rate and a 2025 rate both mean 'how far from that year's mean'. No era term is added.
split: TEMPORAL — train on target season <= 2018, test strictly after
vs_other_sports: tennis +0.0941 over 0.7486, hoops +0.0625 over 0.4514, equities ~0 over 0.85-0.92. The GAINS are not comparable across sports — different targets, baselines and domains — and quoting one against another would be the apples-to-oranges this repo keeps refusing to make.

CORRECTION_why_per_position_prose_number.reading: 0.7642 appears in NO field of this file, and the per-position range is 0.4914-0.7731, not 0.58-0.74. Both numbers read as prose written against an earlier version of the report and not updated when it was regenerated.
CORRECTION_why_per_position_prose_number.the_claim_survives_and_is_stronger: The point of the sentence is that pooling inflates persistence because a ridge can recover position. With the current fields that gap is LARGER than the prose claims: pooled 0.8 against per-position 0.4914 to 0.7731, versus the 0.7642 against 0.58-0.74 the sentence asserts.
CORRECTION_why_per_position_prose_number.no_published_number_is_affected: dumbmodel.com's gridiron page does not cite 0.7642 (grep count 0). It cites QB persistence 0.4914, which is a real field.
